title: Safe automatic repair for allowlisted docs/status integration sync conflicts
description: Implement the Oracle Workflow result for Ralph CLI itself. Fix Ralph so low-risk integration sync conflicts in status documents such as docs/TODO.md and docs/PROJECT-STATUS.md do not permanently block the queue. Ralph must not weaken merge safety for code, config, schema, migrations, security-sensitive files, or lockfiles, and must not perform automatic ours/theirs winner selection. Instead, add a narrow deterministic docs resolver that preserves both sides' facts, records proof, exposes a manual repair-conflicts command, and lets manager auto-recovery try the resolver before stopping with merge_repair_integration_sync_conflict. Use the complete Oracle bundle at /Users/shawn/.ralph-prds/ralph-cli/oracle-conflict-resolver-full-bundle.md as candidate-only reference; Ralph must validate, adapt, test, and repair against the actual checkout.

userStories.title: Deterministically resolve allowlisted status-doc conflicts
userStories.description: As a Ralph operator, I want integration-sync conflicts limited to docs/TODO.md and docs/PROJECT-STATUS.md to be repaired by a deterministic union/preservation resolver so low-risk status-doc drift does not block the whole queue.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolver only runs when every conflict file is allowlisted and under configured size/count limits.
Resolver removes Git conflict markers and preserves facts from both sides of every conflict hunk.
Resolver refuses code/config/schema/migration/security/lockfile/binary conflicts and leaves the existing blocked_by_policy/manual path intact.
Resolver does not use git checkout --ours, git checkout --theirs, or equivalent whole-file winner selection.
Resolver includes deterministic handling for docs/TODO.md and docs/PROJECT-STATUS.md and can safely union TODO bullets, checkbox entries, table rows, headings, and status facts.

userStories.title: Expose repair-conflicts CLI command
userStories.description: As an operator, I can run ralph repair-conflicts <task-id> --dry-run or --apply to inspect and safely apply deterministic docs conflict repair.
acceptanceCriteria: A repair-conflicts command is wired into the CLI.
Command supports --dry-run, --apply, --json, and --allow-llm flags.
--dry-run reports eligibility, files, retained-fact counts, warnings, and candidate proof without writing files.
--apply writes the resolved files, stages them, commits the integration-sync merge when appropriate, records proof, and reports the exact mergeability probe result where available.
LLM mode remains optional and disabled or safely stubbed for this first slice; deterministic repair is sufficient.

userStories.title: Manager auto-recovery tries docs repair before policy stop
userStories.description: As a queue user, I want the Ralph manager to attempt safe deterministic repair for eligible docs/status integration-sync conflicts before declaring a manual policy block.
acceptanceCriteria: recoverFailedWorkerMergeRepairTasks or the equivalent manager recovery path calls the shared resolver when the exact probe fails in integration_sync.
Successful repair writes an integration_sync_conflict_auto_resolved event and TaskConflictRepairProof evidence.
If repair is ineligible, unsafe, or post-repair probe still cannot prove a clean state, manager keeps the existing stopped/manual policy path.
The manager does not duplicate large finalize/promotion logic unnecessarily; it may record repair and let the next manager loop reuse existing clean-probe recovery.

The current ez4ielts scenario with docs/TODO.md and docs/PROJECT-STATUS.md can be auto-repaired or manually repaired by command without dropping either side; after repair, retry/manager recovery can proceed and unblock the pending overlapping UI QA task.

userStories.title: Proof and queue messaging make the safety boundary explicit
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I can tell from task state and queue output whether a conflict is auto-repairable docs drift or still a policy-blocked unsafe conflict.
acceptanceCriteria: Task state can record conflict repair proof with strategy, resolver version, conflict files, before/after hashes, retained fact counts, dropped facts, warnings, commit SHA, and exact probe result when available.
Queue messaging for eligible integration-sync docs conflicts points operators to repair-conflicts --dry-run/--apply instead of only saying manual repair.
Queue policy still reports that automatic conflict winner selection is prohibited.
Repair context hints mention repair-conflicts only when all conflict files are allowlisted status docs.

userStories.title: Regression tests protect the conflict safety model
userStories.description: As a Ralph maintainer, I want tests proving allowlisted docs can be repaired and unsafe conflicts still refuse.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover TODO union/checkbox preservation.
Tests cover PROJECT-STATUS status fact preservation.
Tests cover repair-conflicts or core resolver apply path for allowlisted docs.
Tests cover refusal for non-doc/code conflicts.
Tests cover manager recovery attempting docs repair before stopping integration_sync conflicts.
npm run build and npm test pass or Ralph records specific pre-existing baseline failures separately from task-induced failures.
The full Oracle candidate implementation in /Users/shawn/.ralph-prds/ralph-cli/oracle-conflict-resolver-full-bundle.md is consulted and either applied or consciously adapted.
No automatic ours/theirs winner selection is introduced anywhere.
No secrets, local user state, or unrelated dirty working tree changes are committed by this task.

Given docs/TODO.md conflict where both sides add different TODO bullets, repair-conflicts --apply keeps both bullets, removes conflict markers, records evidence, and permits the exact mergeability probe to proceed.
Given docs/PROJECT-STATUS.md conflict where both sides add task status entries, resolver preserves both entries and produces stable output.
Given same TODO item with conflicting states, resolver preserves both facts or emits a conservative combined note; it must not silently discard either side.

Given any conflict outside the docs/status allowlist, including src/*.ts, lockfiles, migrations, schema, config, or security-sensitive files, resolver refuses and queue remains blocked_by_policy/manual_repair.

Every applied repair writes TaskConflictRepairProof or equivalent evidence with conflict files, strategy, before/after hashes, retained-fact counts, droppedFacts, warnings, commit SHA, and exact-probe result when available.
Manager auto-recovery attempts deterministic docs conflict repair before stopping with merge_repair_integration_sync_conflict.
The built CLI exposes repair-conflicts in help output.
externalDependencies: Node.js and npm available for npm run build and npm test.
Git available in test fixtures and integration worktrees.
Current ralph-cli main working tree may contain unrelated dirty changes; Ralph must work in its own task worktree and must not revert those changes.
The global ralph binary may be built from /Users/shawn/Project/ralph-cli/dist/cli.js; after implementation Ralph should run npm run build before using the new command.
The ez4ielts blocked queue can be used as a manual scenario after the Ralph CLI build includes repair-conflicts.

referenceImplementation.applyInstructions: Read the complete Oracle Markdown bundle. Apply the candidate code only if compatible with the actual checkout; otherwise adapt it. The PRD acceptance criteria are authoritative. Preserve existing unrelated work and do not revert dirty main-worktree changes. If the Oracle patch references APIs that differ in the live repo, repair against the live repo with focused tests.
assumptions: The first implementation slice is deterministic and narrow; LLM fallback can be a safe stub.
docs/TODO.md and docs/PROJECT-STATUS.md are treated as status docs where union/preservation is safer than winner selection.
Ralph's existing clean-probe recovery path can complete the state transition after an auto-repair event if immediate promotion would require duplicating complex logic.
The candidate bundle was generated from a dirty live source snapshot and may need adaptation to the task worktree baseline.
knownRisks: The ralph-cli repo currently has unrelated dirty changes in the main worktree; Ralph may need to adapt the Oracle candidate to HEAD rather than the dirty snapshot.
If existing tests or public APIs changed since the attached Oracle files, the candidate patches may need manual repair by Ralph.
Automatic docs union can preserve stale facts; this is acceptable only for the allowlisted status-doc first slice and should be explicit in proof warnings.
The new repair-conflicts command must be built before it can be used to unblock the existing ez4ielts queue.
If the ez4ielts integration worktree has been cleaned and no conflict markers remain, repair-conflicts must reconstruct or re-run the configured integration sync safely rather than guessing.
